title: Chicken Rice (Simplified version)
description: Chicken and rice cooked together in a ginger-garlic stock, with a fresh chilli sauce on the side.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of traditional chicken rice with sliced poached chicken, rice, cucumber and chilli sauce.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · traditional chicken rice · displayed crop
personalNote: Chilli sauce for bubu and soy sauce for dudu. Be gentle with the rice at the end, Jack—this is the bit where we fluff it rather than squish it.
equipment: Large pot with a close-fitting lid
Fine sieve or bowl for washing rice
Heat-safe container for cooling the stock
advancePrep: Check the freezer for ginger-garlic blocks. Four blocks can replace the fresh garlic and ginger for the pot, and one block can replace the garlic and ginger for the chilli sauce.
importantNotes: This makes four portions. Remember to take the stock out for our chilli sauce before the rice goes in. Keep the lid on for the final 10-minute rest. The prep and cooking times are estimates.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.note: Use 500–600 g for our four-portion batch; chop into small pieces.

ingredients.name: Garlic for the pot
ingredients.note: Peel and chop finely. Can be replaced together with the ginger by 4 ginger-garlic blocks for our batch.

ingredients.name: Ginger for the pot
ingredients.note: A large piece; peel and chop as finely as you can. Omit if using the ginger-garlic blocks.

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.note: Dice, or replace with a bunch of spring onions. Clean spring onions carefully to remove any grit.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.note: Wash in cold water three times if possible.

ingredients.name: Garlic for the chilli sauce
ingredients.note: Or replace this and the ginger with 1 ginger-garlic block for our batch.

ingredients.name: Ginger for the chilli sauce
ingredients.note: A piece the same size as the garlic clove; omit if using a ginger-garlic block.

ingredients.name: Cooked chicken stock
ingredients.note: Take from the pot after the covered 20-minute boil, before adding rice.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics and chicken
steps.description: Check the freezer first, Jack: if we have ginger-garlic blocks, use those instead of chopping the fresh garlic and ginger. Otherwise peel and chop both as small as you can. Dice the red onion, or clean and chop the spring onions properly so we don’t get sand in the food. Chop the chicken into small pieces and boil the measured water.
steps.tip: Clean spring onions thoroughly: trapped sand gives the finished food a gritty texture.

steps.title: Cook the chicken with the aromatics
steps.description: Put the chicken, garlic, ginger and onion in the pot. Squish them around on medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until the chicken goes white on the outside.
steps.warning: This first colour change does not mean the chicken is cooked through. It will continue cooking in the stock.

steps.title: Add the stock ingredients and boil
steps.description: Add the turmeric, chicken stock cube, boiled water and light soy sauce. Bring it to the boil, put the lid on and let it boil for 20 minutes.
steps.tip: While this cooks, wash the rice and prepare the chilli sauce ingredients.

steps.title: Wash the rice and prepare the chilli ingredients
steps.description: While that’s going, wash the rice in cold water three times if you can, then drain it. This helps it stay grainy instead of mushing together. Get the chilli-sauce garlic, equal-sized piece of ginger, birds-eye chillies and lime juice ready too. A ginger-garlic block can replace the fresh garlic and ginger for the sauce.
steps.tip: Washing removes excess starch so the rice grains stay more separate.

steps.title: Save stock for the chilli sauce
steps.description: After the 20 minutes, check the chicken is cooked through, then take out the stock measured for our chilli sauce BEFORE adding the rice. Let that stock cool before blending. I like to help it cool by standing a heat-safe container in a bowl of cold water.
steps.tip: Only use stock from the cooked pot for the chilli sauce.
steps.warning: Check the chicken is cooked through before taking out the sauce stock. If using a thermometer, the centre should reach 75°C for 30 seconds. Follow your blender’s instructions about hot liquids.

steps.title: Cook the rice in the pot
steps.description: Add the washed, drained rice. Put the lid back on and cook for 15 minutes on medium-low heat.

steps.title: Rest with the lid on
steps.description: Turn the heat off now, but don’t open the lid yet. Leave it alone for 10 minutes so the rice can finish resting in the steam.
steps.tip: Keep the steam inside the pot while the rice rests.

steps.title: Blend the chilli sauce
steps.description: Blend the chilli-sauce garlic, ginger, chillies, cooled stock and lime juice. It doesn’t need to be perfectly smooth. If you’re using our ginger-garlic block, use that instead of the fresh garlic and ginger.
steps.warning: Let the stock cool before blending.

steps.title: Fluff gently and serve
steps.description: Open the lid and gently fluff the rice. Try not to squish it around here or the grains will break and get mushy. Chilli sauce for bubu, soy sauce for dudu, and we’re ready to eat.
steps.tip: Lift and loosen the rice gently instead of pressing or mashing it.

substitutions.title: Freezer ginger-garlic blocks
substitutions.text: For the original four-serving batch, use 4 blocks instead of the head of garlic and 50 g ginger in the pot. Use 1 block instead of the garlic clove and equal-sized ginger piece in the chilli sauce.

substitutions.title: Spring onions instead of red onion
substitutions.text: Use a bunch of spring onions. Clean them properly before chopping so sand does not get into the food.

troubleshooting.title: Avoiding mushy rice
troubleshooting.text: Wash the rice three times if possible. Let it rest with the lid on, then fluff gently instead of squishing it around.

troubleshooting.title: Chilli sauce texture
troubleshooting.text: It does not have to be completely smooth; a little texture is fine.

storage: For leftovers, divide the rice and chicken into small containers and cool quickly, ideally within 1 hour. Refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.
reheating: Reheat the rice and chicken once, until steaming hot throughout. Stir or turn it when microwaving so there are no cold pockets.
foodSafety: Chicken must be fully cooked before its stock is used in the chilli sauce. A thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Keep utensils used for raw chicken away from the sauce ingredients and finished food.
servingSuggestion: Chilli sauce for bubu and soy sauce for dudu. Gently fluff the rice before serving.
